mission: Ben encounters Aevyn directly or semi-directly. No full fight yet. Aevyn reveals personal knowledge of Jacen and unsettles Ben.
why_now: Aevyn found Ben before Ben was ready — likely because Aevyn felt the Force probe from the ridge and chose to surface on his own terms rather than wait. Ben has no backup, no cover, and no script for this conversation.
conflict: Ben needs information about the cache and what Aevyn has already done with it, but every question he asks confirms to Aevyn that Ben does not know enough yet — and Aevyn has no reason to help him catch up unless he wants something from Ben in return.
turning_point: Aevyn confirms Jacen left something near the Glasswell.
closing_hook: Aevyn confirms Jacen left something near the Glasswell.
setting: Iresh, near the Glasswell — a wind-scoured shelf above the cavern entrance. Cold, exposed, gray sky. Ben and Aevyn meet directly for the first time. No blades drawn; the threat is in the air between them, not on display. The Kathol Rift is a distant reference point that gives the shelf its weight: this is the kind of waypoint Jacen used — a world at the edge of charted space, chosen for that reason.

stakes.personal: Aevyn looks at Ben and sees Jacen’s primary student — everything Aevyn was not, in the body of someone who apparently abandoned the lessons anyway. Ben looks at Aevyn and has to work to not recognize the anger underneath the control, because it is too close to something he has felt himself.
stakes.interpersonal: Aevyn does not explain himself and does not need to — he speaks to Ben as someone who shares context Ben does not want acknowledged. The asymmetry is the threat: Aevyn knows what Jacen showed him privately, and Ben cannot pretend that does not matter.
stakes.external: Ben needs to know how far Aevyn has gotten with the cache without tipping his hand — and Aevyn confirms the holocron is near the Glasswell without telling Ben anything useful about the timeline.

sensory_details: The shelf above the Glasswell entrance: cold exposed stone, wind unbroken by any shelter, the low drone of the Glasswell itself audible through the rock underfoot. Aevyn’s lightsaber is clipped but visible — the housing slightly asymmetrical, a self-built thing. His equipment is carried with the practical organization of someone who trained in field operations, not mystic rites. One concrete anchor: when Aevyn names the Aing-Tii of the Kathol Rift as the source of flow-walking — the root of what he calls Recognition — he says it the way a man recites the thing that gave his life meaning. No reverence in his tone. Just precision. That is what unsettles Ben: it sounds like scholarship, and scholarship is harder to argue with than conviction.

turning_point_detail.trigger: Aevyn uses a Recognition-adjacent technique — not a full weaponized application, just a directed noticing — to surface one specific detail from Ben's past: the corridor moment, reversed. He does not describe it; he describes what Ben was doing wrong with a stance Jacen corrected at fourteen, in language Jacen used. The knowledge is too precise to be guessed.
turning_point_detail.shift: Ben understands that Aevyn was there — not as a stranger, but as another student, close enough to have watched Jacen teach. The ground shifts: Aevyn is not reading files. He was present.
turning_point_detail.cost: Aevyn confirms Jacen left the holocron near the Glasswell and ends the conversation on his terms. He does not threaten. He does not need to.

emotional_arc.start: Ben approaches the conversation as an investigation — he wants intelligence, he is willing to be direct, and he is prepared for a threat. What he is not prepared for is recognition.
emotional_arc.shift: Aevyn uses Jacen-specific private knowledge to establish he is not a Vigil operative who read a file — he was trained by the same person. Ben has to reorganize what he thought this encounter was.
emotional_arc.end: Ben ends the conversation unsettled in a specific way: not afraid of Aevyn physically, but aware that Aevyn sees the GAG-trained part of him that no one else acknowledges, and that being seen that clearly is its own kind of danger.

key_beats.beat_description: Aevyn surfaces on the exposed shelf above the Glasswell entrance — he chose the meeting, chose the ground, and stands completely unhurried.
key_beats.state_change: The terms of the encounter are already set before Ben speaks — Aevyn controls the frame.
key_beats.pov_reaction: the adjustment of reading a space that was already arranged against him; not fear, a recalibration of posture

key_beats.beat_description: Aevyn establishes in the first exchange that he knows Ben as Jacen's student and as a former GAG operative — not from files, from shared context.
key_beats.state_change: Ben's categories for this encounter (antagonist, operative, stranger) do not hold — Aevyn is something closer.
key_beats.pov_reaction: the slight forward lean of someone hearing their own history named accurately; wariness that cannot be resolved by denial

key_beats.beat_description: Aevyn uses a precise detail from Jacen's private instruction — language Jacen used for a correction at fourteen — to establish he was present in the same apprenticeship world.
key_beats.state_change: Ben understands Aevyn was not reading a file; he was there, secondary but present, watching the same lessons.
key_beats.pov_reaction: the ground shifting; the specific vertigo of a stranger knowing something that was private

key_beats.beat_description: Ben recognizes that Aevyn's wound is not ideology but placement — not chosen, only useful, years spent proving Jacen was wrong to treat him as secondary.
key_beats.state_change: The encounter's emotional logic becomes legible: Aevyn's grievance is comprehensible, which makes it harder to dismiss.
key_beats.pov_reaction: a recognition he does not want to complete; the pull to understand resisted because understanding here is dangerous

key_beats.beat_description: Aevyn confirms the holocron is near the Glasswell and ends the conversation on his terms.
key_beats.state_change: Ben has the confirmation he came for and has given up nothing useful — but Aevyn has established that he sees the GAG-trained part of Ben that no one else names.
key_beats.pov_reaction: not relief at having information — unease at having been read; the exposure of being seen clearly by the wrong person

canon_elements_needed: Aing-Tii / Kathol Rift: flow-walking as the root technique behind Recognition — Aevyn places the holocron in this lineage as cold scholarship, not mysticism
Fallanassi / White Current: Holding's other root strand — one strand, not named at length, enough to confirm Aevyn knows the full lineage
Vergere: the third teacher Jacen synthesized — Aevyn's knowledge of all three confirms he was a genuine student, not an imitator reading files
notes:
Source: Chapter Outlines v4.1. Act: Act Three — Iresh / Glasswell / Aevyn. Chapter title: The Other Student.

Character voice focus: preserve the exact v1.4 character behavior and dialogue rules for the chapter POV and named participants. Plot first, character second, theme through consequences.

Drafter texture cue: Aevyn places the holocron's lineage in three beats — Aing-Tii (flow-walking, the root), Fallanassi / White Current (Holding's strand), Vergere (the synthesis) — each name dropped once, flat, the way someone names the authors of a field rather than the names of gods. One term, one consequence: Ben's consequence is that Aevyn knows Jacen the way a true student does, and that knowledge is not borrowed from a file. Weaponized Recognition here is just being seen accurately. Do not editorialize; let the precision do the work.
